metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that are consistent with the Tallying heuristic on trials where Tallying makes a strict prediction (i.e., one option has more feature-wise wins than the other). The experimental design explicitly pits Tallying against WADD on these trials: Tallying chooses the option with more small wins, whereas WADD chooses the option with a single massive win on a heavily weighted feature. Consequently, data simulated under Tallying will yield a metric value close to 1.0, while data simulated under WADD will yield a value close to 0.0.

Trial 4 and Trial 1 are perfectly opposed for WADD versus Tallying. In Trial 4 (A=[5, 0, 0, 0], B=[0, 1, 1, 1]), WADD strongly prefers A due to the high validity of the first cue and its large magnitude difference, whereas Tallying prefers B because it wins on 3 out of 4 features. In Trial 1 (A=[0, 4, 4, 4], B=[5, 3, 3, 3]), WADD prefers B due to the first cue, while Tallying prefers A because A wins on 3 features. The metric calculates the difference in the probability of choosing A between Trial 4 and Trial 1. WADD predicts a value near +1, while Tallying predicts a value near -1.
